The direction vector of the first line is  
\[
\vec d_1=(-3,-2,-6).
\]
The direction vector of the second line is  
\[
\vec d_2=(1,2,2).
\]

For the acute angle \(\theta\) between the lines,
\[
\cos\theta=\frac{|\vec d_1\cdot \vec d_2|}{|\vec d_1||\vec d_2|}.
\]

Compute the dot product:
\[
\vec d_1\cdot \vec d_2=(-3)(1)+(-2)(2)+(-6)(2)=-3-4-12=-19.
\]
So
\[
|\vec d_1\cdot \vec d_2|=19.
\]

Now compute the magnitudes:
\[
|\vec d_1|=\sqrt{(-3)^2+(-2)^2+(-6)^2}=\sqrt{9+4+36}=\sqrt{49}=7,
\]
\[
|\vec d_2|=\sqrt{1^2+2^2+2^2}=\sqrt{1+4+4}=\sqrt{9}=3.
\]

Thus,
\[
\cos\theta=\frac{19}{7\cdot 3}=\frac{19}{21}.
\]
